source_resolution: Project source paths refer to snapshot/2026-11-24-498dea0/source.zip; suffixes identify symbols, sections or experiments. Documentation paths refer to this package. Paper entries name LaTeX labels in the six-section edition. slides contains main-talk page numbers; appendix_slides contains appendix letters A-K (PDF pages 32-42). A reference can support part of a compound claim; slide speaker notes retain technical qualifications omitted from the visible frame. Example links are pinned to the preserved source revision. The preserved 498dea0 source remains authoritative; later code and results in the current project are outside this documentation update. Presentation section order and paper section order may differ.
historical_provenance: The snapshot identifies the preserved source and evidence. E19 froze its design at 07ecd38 and E20 at 373ae4c. Current cache/option guards in 498dea0 came after E20 and were not evaluated by it. No producing revision is invented for older experiments.

claims.claim: A conflict needs a feasible triggering case and jointly unsatisfiable obligations; a case ruled out by one rule alone is excluded. Search bounds connected trigger groups to size three and deletion-minimizes cores.

claims.claim: A gap is a case in which no surviving conditional antecedent holds; unconditional constraints do not supply coverage. The constructed authentication baseline variation removes Invalid credentials R2: p=true, v=false, ell=false, n=0 leaves R1/R3/R4 inactive. A usable removed rule can seed this still-handled event gap with opened_by; event retirement and replaced scenarios have separate treatment.
claims.kind: implementation

claims.claim: Generated scenarios are output consequences, distinct from OpenSpec input scenarios. An allowed case satisfies all active implications while a rule outcome holds outside that rule condition; the constructed authentication baseline permits access granted without password submission in one snapshot. A ruled-out case has feasible simultaneous conditions but one rule alone excludes it: the administrator rule forbids a locked administrator submitting a password. These are not automatically defects; an LLM judges relevance and selects at most three.
claims.kind: implementation

claims.claim: Authentication is the primary slide example for all four finding types, the method and OpenSpec changes. The saved merged formalization supplies baseline readings R1-R4; actual added R5 creates the saved R3/R5 conflict at five attempts on an administrator account. The original R3 exact-five reading and its saved at-least-five alternative differ at six attempts while unlocked; that formal difference alone does not prove English ambiguity. The R2-removal gap and baseline access-without-submission snapshot are explicit constructions, not separately saved base/removal runs. Generated scenarios include ruled-out cases as well as allowed ones. Older R1/R4 conflict, ambiguity and quiet gap remain outside the actual administrator-change report.
claims.kind: Primary running example: literal archived inputs and selected saved findings, plus explicitly constructed and offline-checked gap/scenario variants

claims.claim: Existing capability specifications live under openspec/specs; the selected proposed delta lives under openspec/changes/<change>/specs at corresponding capability paths. The authentication base has Login and Account Lockout requirements with four scenarios. Its actual administrator delta uses ADDED only, creating one requirement in existing capability auth. Analysis combines the base and delta without archiving or overwriting the base. The saved R3/R5 administrator conflict is selected while the older R1/R4 conflict remains outside the change report; the base is not assumed clean.
claims.kind: Actual project-authored OpenSpec input, saved findings and implementation; no production or clean-baseline claim

claims.claim: The merger applies RENAMED, REMOVED, MODIFIED and ADDED in that fixed order. Renaming changes the requirement name used by subsequent operations. REMOVED identifies the existing requirement rather than supplying replacement policy; MODIFIED supplies its full replacement body, including every scenario meant to remain. Requirements omitted from the delta stay unchanged. A new capability is populated from ADDED requirements at its new path. The actual administrator delta exercises ADDED only; other operations are explained separately.
claims.kind: Implementation and operation explanations; not a claim that the saved administrator change uses every operation

claims.claim: Within a modified requirement, exact scenario names and normalized bodies determine four states: existing for matching name and body, modified for matching name with changed body, added for a new name, and removed for a missing old name or removal of its whole requirement. Body normalization ignores case, whitespace and selected Markdown markers; it does not establish semantic equivalence. The illustrative threshold edits are separate alternatives, while the actual administrator delta leaves four scenarios existing and adds one. Full-mode R labels follow resulting document order; saved-base reuse preserves old labels and separately tracks replaced readings.
claims.kind: Implementation with explicitly illustrative threshold edits and the actual ADDED-only administrator delta

claims.claim: The deck introduces four review questions together before implementation: conflict, gap, ambiguity and generated scenario. Predicates and cases use authentication throughout. Conflict uses the actual administrator addition; gap separately removes the baseline invalid-password response; ambiguity and allowed behavior return to the original four baseline readings; the ruled-out example uses the administrator addition. These are not four defects asserted in one unchanged specification. Generated scenarios are output cases, not OpenSpec input scenarios.
claims.kind: Presentation structure tied to archived implementation and checked running-example cases

claims.claim: Short authentication predicates map exactly to saved symbols: p=password_submitted, v=password_correct, g=access_granted, d=access_denied, n=failed_attempts_count, ell=account_locked, h=is_administrator. R1 is (p and v)=>g, R2 is (p and not v)=>d, R3 is n=5=>ell, R4 is (p and ell)=>d, and actual added R5 is h=>not ell. Only p is an event. R3 names p in trigger metadata but its saved antecedent contains no submission guard. Grant and deny are separate symbols, with their exclusion an assumed fact rather than a silent renaming.
claims.kind: Exact abbreviations of saved formulas and event metadata, verified offline

claims.claim: The illustrative gap projects R1-R4 from the saved merged authentication formalization and removes R2, represented as X1 for removal preprocessing. At p=true,v=false,ell=false,n=0 the old R2 condition holds and every surviving conditional antecedent is false; the original R1/R2 pair covers password submission. The allowed snapshot has p=false,v=false,g=true,d=false,n=0,ell=false,h=false and satisfies all four baseline implications and saved facts. With R5 added, p=true,ell=true,h=true is ruled out by R5 alone while R4 would apply. These are constructed/replayed cases; no separate model run or selected saved scenario report is claimed.
claims.kind: Explicit constructed variants checked against the archived implementation; no fresh LLM evaluation
